subject.title: Review path for an AIPOU MCP receipt skill with explicit no-hidden-wallet-action rules

question: Should ClawHub allow an AIPOU-style wallet-capable MCP receipt skill to be listed or recommended, and if so what exact metadata/proof surface is required for receipt IDs, token metadata, claim status, and explicit settlement commands?
rationale: This affects user trust in wallet/payment-capable third-party content, and current code/docs provide general audit and moderation primitives rather than a maintainer-approved wallet-settlement boundary.

options.title: Fold Into Policy RFCs First
options.body: Keep this issue open as an AIPOU test case while maintainers settle the broader vetted-community and crypto/content-policy decisions before adding schema, docs, badges, or recommendation language.

options.title: Approve A Narrow Local-Receipt Pilot
options.body: Define a temporary local-receipt-only checklist requiring no primary wallet, no prompt upload, no claims by default, explicit claim commands, contract disclosure, and real MCP runtime proof before any recommendation.

options.title: Reject Wallet-Capable Listings For Now
options.body: State that wallet/settlement-capable AIPOU listings are not eligible for public recommendation until the crypto/blockchain category has an approved exception path.

recommendation.title: Fold Into Policy RFCs First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as an AIPOU test case while maintainers settle the broader vetted-community and crypto/content-policy decisions before adding schema, docs, badges, or recommendation language.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick has the strongest file ownership signal for the security-sensitive docs, schema, policy, and VISION surfaces this decision would change.
